Model: Chords. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/10 Chords
Type: 1 (stored choice code). Inv/Transp: 0.391. Shape control: 0.455.

Type chooses the chord; Inv/Transp changes its inversion and register; Shape changes the oscillator waveform. The chord keeps its identity as Inv/Transp changes. Chords mode uses the last key as the root and disables paraphony. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/10 Chords

Play a root note to trigger the oscillator’s chord, then use Timbre to change the voicing. The saved envelope opens the low-pass filter on each note; pressure or velocity can add further cutoff modulation according to the global keyboard-expression setting. The small LFO-to-Timbre route adds movement to the inversion. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/10 Chords · Microfreak/UG/05 Connections/02 Matrix and Encoder/01 Sources and Destinations

Fight comes in as a lead at 07:01 in GitP/A/Session/26/10/26-Mon, announced on the commentary microphone as “118” followed by an indistinct word. No knobs move for the next 50 seconds; pad pressure carries the movement through the PRESSURE → Cutoff route. From 07:51, Wave and Timbre changes on that layer step through chord types and inversions. The saved capture supplies a factory baseline, not evidence of unsaved edits.

Model: Noise. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/13 Noise

Wave morphs particle noise through white noise to metallic noise. Timbre changes noise sample-rate reduction and the pitch of the metallic component; Shape blends the noise with a pitched waveform. The saved cycling-envelope routes sweep both noise character controls, while keyboard tracking counteracts part of the Timbre movement. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/13 Noise

Hold several notes in paraphonic mode to hear the noise-and-pitched blend across the keyboard. The looping Cycling Envelope sweeps noise character while key position changes Timbre and cutoff. The LFO modulates its own rate and the Cycling Envelope’s amount and fall, so the saved modulation wiring can produce changing motion without manual knob turns. The saved factory baseline does not capture those unsaved changes.

Play single notes low on the keyboard. Each note starts a short main-envelope pluck that opens the low-pass filter and, through the negative ENV → Wave route, pulls the waveform and timbre on the attack. The looping Cycling Envelope at high amount adds a repeating pulse, and the small glide joins legato notes. Pressure brightens the timbre. Microfreak/UG/05 Connections/02 Matrix and Encoder/01 Sources and Destinations · Microfreak/UG/09 Envelope Gen/06 Cycling Envelope

Hold a note while the cycling envelope moves speech formants and the filtered random LFO changes Word and pulls the low-pass cutoff downward. These saved routes couple changing syllables with changing brightness. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/11 Speech

Expression raises filter resonance and the Arp/Seq Rate assignment. The rate route affects note repetition when the arpeggiator or sequencer is running; its presence alone does not establish that either was active in a performance. Hold a note and let the slow main-envelope attack bring the noise in. With Shape saved at zero, the Noise model starts from noise alone; Wave selects the noise character and Timbre applies sample-rate reduction. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/13 Noise

The Cycling Envelope moves noise Wave, Timbre and band-pass cutoff together. The slow filtered random LFO varies the envelope Rise and Fall settings, so the saved modulation changes the pace of those sweeps. The matrix has no nonzero pressure or keyboard modulation routes. Model: V.Analog. Detune sets the detuning between two waves; Shape morphs a variable square from narrow pulse through full square to hard-sync formants; Wave morphs a saw from triangle to sawtooth with a widening notch. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/06 VAnalog

On the panel, V.Analog puts Detune on the Wave knob (CC 10), Shape on the Timbre knob (CC 12) and Wave on the Shape knob (CC 13). In the session codekiln worked this out by ear: "So timbre is the shape."
Detune: 0.013. Shape: 0.024. Wave: 0.175. The saved sound starts almost undetuned, with a narrow pulse and a mostly triangular wave.
Pitch bend range: stored as 12; the unit is not verified.
Keyboard octave: +2, per the MicroFreak Reader octave table. Glide: 0.
Low-pass filter. Saved cutoff: 0.099; resonance: 0.000. Cutoff and resonance are normalized settings, not hertz or display values. Microfreak/UG/07 Filter/01 Modifying Sound/01 Low Pass Filter

The main envelope opens the low-pass cutoff from its low saved setting. The cycling envelope changes resonance independently, emphasizing the cutoff region as the note develops (see the modulation matrix).

Main envelope: attack 0.431, decay/release 0.672, sustain 0.996. Amp Mod is on, so the main envelope controls loudness: notes swell in and hold at nearly full level. Microfreak/UG/09 Envelope Gen/03 Envelope Stages

Cycling Envelope mode: Loop. Stored RiseLvl 0.000, RiseSlp 0.500, FallLvl 0.211, FallSlp 0.500, Hold 0.000, Amount 0.695. These are normalized stored fields; rise and fall times in milliseconds remain unverified. Microfreak/UG/09 Envelope Gen/06 Cycling Envelope

Sample-and-Hold, clock sync off, so the free rate applies. Stored normalized rate: 0.764; stored division code: 5. The rate is not a hertz reading. Microfreak/UG/08 LFO/01 LFO Shape · Microfreak/UG/08 LFO/02 LFO Rate
Amounts use the signed normalized range −1…+1. The Assign columns resolve to the destinations shown.
PRESSURE → Timbre (V.Analog Shape): +0.669. Pressing harder widens the pulse toward square and sync formants.
ENV → Cutoff: +0.605. The main envelope opens the filter as each note swells in.
Cycling Envelope → Assign 1 → Filter Resonance: +1.000. The looping envelope keeps changing the resonance.
PRESSURE → Assign 2 → LFO Rate: +0.180. Pressure speeds up the Sample-and-Hold steps slightly.
LFO → Assign 3 → Wave: +0.199. Sample-and-Hold steps the saw/triangle morph.
All other saved matrix amounts are zero; nothing routes to pitch.
Play the saved sound with sustained notes and varying pressure. Pressure changes the pulse shape and the LFO speed, while the cycling envelope keeps resonance moving underneath.
Paraphonic mode is on in the saved export. The PRESSURE row uses pressure or velocity according to the instrument's global Utility setting; the export does not establish which one was active.

In GitP/A/Session/26/10/24-Sat, the recorded MIDI shows edits away from this baseline: Wave and Shape sweeps, cycling-envelope rise, fall, hold and amount changes, main-envelope attack, decay and sustain changes, a cutoff raise, and detune from about 10:00. Launchpad pad pressure, recorded as per-note pressure, arrives mainly from 11:00. None of these edits were saved.

Before the recording, codekiln heard pressure "really impact the volume." The saved matrix has no pressure route to level, so that impression may come from the Shape modulation or from the session's edits; the export cannot settle it.
